doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Guest singers: Frank Fontaine and Telly Savalas
summary: Some guests sang poorly, but Frank Fontaine had a delightful Irish tenor voice and Telly Savalas did acceptably on the Burnett show.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Were there certain people that would come in as guests that were of questionable musical talent, that would try singing or whatever.
Sure. I won’t mention any names. And then surprisingly there were some people that you had no idea that they were able to do that. I didn’t. There was a comic named Frank Fontaine.
He was on the Jackie Gleason show.
Yes he did indeed. And he had a delightful voice, which I didn’t know.
Well yeah it was almost like an Irish tenor.

Exactly. That’s correct. I was really impressed with that. And actually, as I recall Telly Savalas sounded pretty good when he sang on the Carol Burnett Show. He did, you know that deep voice and he sort of talked it a bit too, but I thought he did quite an acceptable job. But there were those who would really have a very poor sense of pitch and would either sing painfully flat or sharp, one or the other. But they were popular enough that they accepted it I guess.
